headline: C$3B GUYANA GOLD HUB SEALED — G2/GMIN ARRANGEMENT PASSES SHAREHOLDER VOTE, CLOSE SET FOR EARLY JULY
source_name: GlobeNewswire / G2 Goldfields Inc. (TSXV: GUYGF) + G Mining Ventures Corp. (TSX: GMIN)
snippet: G2 Goldfields shareholders voted today, June 16, 2026 at the Toronto special meeting to approve the plan of arrangement with G Mining Ventures Corp., clearing the final shareholder hurdle for the C$3 billion combination that creates one of the most strategically compelling gold production hubs in South America. With both Institutional Shareholder Services and Glass Lewis having recommended FOR, and with the deal carrying a 72% premium to G2's pre-announcement share price, the outcome was widely anticipated: each G2 share receives 0.212 GMIN shares plus 0.5 shares of G3 Goldfields, a spin-out that retains G2's non-Guyana exploration assets, with the transaction expected to close in early July 2026. The combined Oko West (GMIN, fully permitted and financed) and Oko-Ghanie (G2, adjacent) projects in Guyana's Puruni region will be developed as a unified operation projected to produce more than 500,000 ounces of gold annually over the mine life — with C$1 billion or more in synergies from shared processing infrastructure — positioning GMIN as one of the largest and lowest-cost gold producers in the Americas in a jurisdiction that has established itself as politically stable and mining-permissive at the highest levels of government.

headline: GOLD STEADIES AT $4,309 ON FOMC DAY 1 — ANALYSTS PROJECT $4,516 MONTH-END IF WARSH SOFTENS RATE LANGUAGE WEDNESDAY
snippet: Gold is trading at $4,308.98 as Kevin Warsh's inaugural two-day FOMC meeting opens June 16 — recovered from the $4,165 correction low on the Iran ceasefire tailwind but consolidating 3% below the immediate post-peace rally high of $4,338, with markets in a clear holding pattern ahead of Wednesday's 2 PM ET press conference. Analysts surveyed by CBS News project gold's June 2026 trading range at $4,186–$4,933 per ounce, with a month-end target of $4,516 contingent on the dot plot revealing a softening of the

forward guidance language — a revision the rapid deflation of Iran-driven energy inflation makes analytically defensible without requiring an explicit dovish pivot. The rate hold itself is 97% priced; tomorrow's dot plot and Warsh's first press conference as Fed Chair are the singular information events that will set the precious metals directional bias for Q3 2026.

headline: ENERGY FUELS RACES TO FIRST US URANIUM + HEAVY REE DUAL COMMERCIAL PRODUCTION BY Q4 2026 AT WHITE MESA
source_name: Crux Investor / Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE: UUUU)
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE: UUUU) is targeting commercial-scale separated heavy rare earth element production — dysprosium (Dy), terbium (Tb), and samarium (Sm) at greater than 99.5% purity — at its White Mesa Mill in Utah by Q4 2026, building on the successful July 2025 pilot production of 99.9%-pure Dy oxide and subsequent magnet qualification by a US rare earth magnet manufacturer in December 2025. White Mesa is already the only operating conventional uranium mill in the United States, and once the HREE circuit modifications targeted for completion by mid-2026 are finalized, it would be the only facility in the Western world producing both uranium oxide and separated heavy rare earth element oxides from commercial ore simultaneously — a dual critical mineral production profile no other company currently possesses at commercial scale outside China. For investors tracking the HREE supply chain bifurcation — dysprosium at $930/kg, terbium approaching $4,030/kg in retail ex-China markets while MOFCOM licensing constrains Chinese export availability — Energy Fuels' integrated White Mesa model represents the most advanced US-jurisdiction path to commercial Dy and Tb production that exists today.

headline: NEXGEN ROOK I BREAKS GROUND THIS SUMMER — 30M LB/YR ATHABASCA MINE WILL COVER 20%+ OF GLOBAL URANIUM SUPPLY
snippet: NexGen Energy Ltd.'s Rook I Project — the highest-grade undeveloped uranium deposit in the world, located in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin — is entering the physical construction phase this summer following the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission's March 5, 2026 licence issuance, with the full project team, procurement chain, engineering contractors, and capital structure confirmed in place to begin site preparation and shaft sinking. At full production, approximately four years from the summer 2026 construction commencement, Rook I is designed to produce up to 30 million pounds of U3O8 annually — representing more than 20% of current global uranium fuel supply and over 50% of Western-world supply from a single deposit — at an average head grade more than ten times the industry average. At $86/lb spot and $91.50/lb long-term contract, the economics are established; the supply contribution is 4 years away from impacting a market where utilities are already accelerating contracting ahead of the January 2028 Russian uranium import ban, making the Rook I construction commencement the most consequential uranium supply-side development of the decade for investors tracking the structural supply deficit.

headline: SILVER AT CHEAPEST vs GOLD IN 12 MONTHS — WHY THE JUNE 16 FOMC OPENING IS THE SETUP SILVER BULLS HAVE BEEN WAITING FOR
snippet: A June 15, 2026 analysis at The Phaser argues that the gold:silver ratio touching near 64:1 during the June correction — the most expensive gold has been relative to silver in 12 months — entering the June 16-17 FOMC week represents the historical setup that has preceded silver's most significant outperformance periods in the current bull cycle. The piece identifies a two-layer catalyst: if Warsh's dot plot softens even modestly on forward guidance (specifically removing or diluting the

language, which the rapid deflation of Iran-driven energy inflation makes analytically defensible), silver benefits from both the monetary easing tailwind and its persistent industrial supply deficit — a combination that historically drives silver's outperformance of gold by 2:1 or more during Fed pivot cycles. Silver had already begun recovering from the $65 correction lows to $70.75 on the Iran ceasefire before the FOMC week began, and the gold:silver ratio compression from 64:1 toward 61:1 in a single session on June 15 provided a concrete preview of what a FOMC catalyst release could accelerate.

headline: REAL YIELDS, NOT THE DOT PLOT, ARE GOLD'S REAL SWING FACTOR — DISCOVERY ALERT MAPS THE OVERLOOKED CPI COMPOSITION SHIFT
snippet: Discovery Alert's June 2026 gold analysis identifies the variable most likely to drive gold's next directional move that the consensus pre-FOMC commentary is missing: US real yields — specifically the forward inflation component that inflated May 2026 CPI to 4.2% via a 23.5% energy price surge tied to the Iran conflict, which has now permanently departed the CPI basket following the Strait of Hormuz reopening. The argument runs as follows: gold at $4,309 is priced as if real yields remain elevated through 2026, because the consensus is treating May's 4.2% CPI print as evidence of underlying inflation persistence. But the composition of that 4.2% was almost entirely energy-driven by a now-resolved geopolitical event — meaning the forward CPI trajectory (and therefore the forward real yield) is resetting dramatically lower regardless of Wednesday's dot plot outcome. The analytical implication for TSXV and ASX junior gold investors: the re-rating opportunity doesn't depend on Warsh being dovish tomorrow — it depends on the market correctly pricing the energy inflation extraction from forward CPI, which is already happening in the oil futures strip and will work through to gold valuations on a 4-8 week lag.

headline: GOLDSEEK ASIAN METALS JUNE 15: ASIAN PHYSICAL GOLD BID PERSISTS INTO FOMC WEEK AS SHANGHAI PREMIUM HOLDS AT CORRECTION LOWS
snippet: GoldSeek's Asian Metals Market Update for June 15, 2026 — published on the eve of Kevin Warsh's inaugural FOMC — identifies systematic Asian physical precious metals accumulation at the $4,150–$4,218 support band that distinguishes the current correction from typical speculative-driven reversals: Chinese physical buyers have maintained elevated Shanghai Premium levels through the 25% gold drawdown from January's $5,589 all-time high, consistent with price-insensitive institutional accumulation rather than retail momentum trading. The June 15 update also tracks Asian silver demand in the context of China's January 2026 strategic material reclassification — noting that the reclassification created a bifurcated silver market where Chinese industrial buyers (solar panel manufacturers absorbing 150 million ounces annually) face domestic pricing while ex-China buyers compete for a reduced global tradeable float, creating structurally higher ex-China silver premiums that persist regardless of LBMA spot price movements. For Australian and Canadian mining investors, the persistence of the Asian physical bid through the June correction is the single most important structural validation of the current precious metals bull market: when sovereign and institutional Asian buyers accumulate at the lows rather than selling, the correction's duration shortens and the subsequent recovery leg tends to be sharper.

headline: ANATOMY OF A 25% GOLD CORRECTION — HOW PRECIOUS METALS FELL FROM $5,589 TO $4,165 AND WHY THE STRUCTURAL BID HELD
snippet: AppreciateWealth's June 2026 analysis maps the six-week correction that took gold from its January 28 all-time high of $5,589 to the $4,165 multi-month low — a 25.5% drawdown that registered as the deepest pullback of the current bull market — identifying five sequential macro drivers: the January ATH driven by de-dollarization and Iran geopolitical bid, the February-April consolidation as Warsh's Fed Chair appointment introduced policy uncertainty, the May acceleration driven by 4.2% CPI from Iran-induced energy inflation, the June correction low at $4,165 as December rate hike probability hit 72%, and finally the $170 snap-back on June 15 as the Iran-US ceasefire structurally removed the primary inflation input. The analysis argues that what restores the structural bull is already in motion — not a new catalyst but the removal of a temporary headwind — with energy inflation's CPI contribution deflating rapidly as Strait of Hormuz oil flows normalize, making the $4,150–$4,300 range an accumulation zone rather than a new equilibrium for an asset whose structural demand drivers (central bank buying at 850+ tonnes annually, de-dollarization, China strategic reclassification of silver) are stronger today than at any point during the correction.

headline: 2026 MINING M&A: DISTRICT CONSOLIDATION REPLACES SINGLE-PROJECT DEALS AS MAJORS DEPLOY RECORD FREE CASH FLOW
snippet: Discovery Alert's 2026 mining M&A trend analysis identifies a structural shift from project-level acquisitions — which characterized 2020-2024 — to district-scale consolidation, exemplified by Agnico Eagle's simultaneous C$3.4B assembly of Rupert Resources, Aurion, and B2Gold's Fingold JV across Finland's Central Lapland Greenstone Belt, and G Mining Ventures' C$3B combination of adjacent Guyana projects into a 500,000+ oz/year production hub (vote passed today, June 16). The analytical framework: producers generating record free cash flow at $4,300+/oz gold are deploying capital not to buy individual deposits but to control entire geological systems where the value of adjacent projects compounds non-linearly and shared infrastructure generates the C$500M+ synergy figures that justify premium acquisition multiples. Discovery Alert maps the next district consolidation wave — Canadian gold camps (Red Lake, Abitibi, Timmins), Athabasca Basin uranium, and British Columbia copper-gold systems — where platform assembly is still incomplete and a single senior producer commitment would reprice junior company valuations across an entire camp, with projects within 50km of a recent senior producer transaction representing the highest-probability M&A re-rating candidates in the next 6-12 months.
